cards.title: xv6 Internals: Traps, Scheduling and Sleep/Wakeup
cards.tagline: xv6 traps flip privilege via scause/sepc; swtch saves 14 registers; sleep(chan,lk) must hold lk until it holds p->lock, or a wakeup is lost.

cards.title: Bit Manipulation and Byte Ordering
cards.tagline: Endianness fixes which byte sits lowest in memory; masks, shifts and popcount/ctz tricks manipulate the bits inside each byte.

cards.title: Binary Search Trees
cards.tagline: A BST turns SEARCH into a root-to-leaf walk — O(lg n) on random input, O(n) on sorted input, hence self-balancing variants in practice.

cards.title: Depth-First Search
cards.tagline: DFS stamps discovery/finish times whose nesting proves ancestry, classifies every edge, and detects cycles in Θ(V+E).

cards.title: Deadlock Avoidance: The Banker's Algorithm
cards.tagline: Grant a resource request only if the resulting state still has a safe order in which every thread can finish.

cards.title: Speculative Execution Attacks: Spectre and Meltdown
cards.tagline: Mistrain a predictor, let a bounds check run speculatively, then read the secret off which cache line got warm.

cards.title: Stacks, Queues and Ring Buffers
cards.tagline: One sequence, two disciplines: LIFO stacks and FIFO queues, built from arrays, linked lists, ring buffers, or two stacks glued together.

cards.title: Dynamic Programming Foundations
cards.tagline: DP = optimal substructure + overlapping subproblems; rod cutting shows the Θ(n²) table and the choice array that reconstructs the cuts.

cards.title: Signals
cards.tagline: Signals are one-bit-per-type notices delivered on return to user mode; never queued, and only async-signal-safe calls belong in a handler.

cards.title: Cache Performance Analysis: AMAT and the Memory Hierarchy
cards.tagline: AMAT = hit time + miss rate × miss penalty, applied recursively L1→L2→L3→DRAM: a small top-level miss-rate cut beats a big DRAM latency cut.

cards.title: Disjoint-Set Forests: Union by Rank and Path Compression
cards.tagline: Union by rank + path compression make m union-find operations cost O(m·α(n)) — effectively linear, and provably optimal.
